newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn declines comment on Hesse remarks on France.
newsitem.headline: Bonn declines comment on Hesse remarks on France.

text.p: The Finance Ministry declined to comment on Friday on remarks by Bundesbank council member Helmut Hesse that the first head of the European Central Bank (ECB) could not be French.
A ministry spokeswoman said there was no reason to start debate over personnel decisions that were not yet imminent.

She noted that European Union finance ministers had decided at their December meeting in Dublin to name Dutch central bank president Wim Duisenberg president of the European Monetary Institute (EMI), the forerunner of the ECB.

Hesse, who is also head of the Landeszentralbank Niedersachsen, said late on Thursday it was "absolutely impossible" that someone from France would become the first head of the ECB, because he could not be unanimously elected by all members of European economic and monetary union (EMU).
In response to recent French criticism of the Bundesbank, Hesse said that of all EU members, France was the most economically vulnerable, since it had not adapted early enough to globalisation.
France is now looking for a scapegoat, and has attempted to make one out of the Bundesbank and its alleged "deflationary policies," he said.
